featured_reviews.name: ashok mukherjee
featured_reviews.review_text:
Happy experience...
Thanks doctors....

Yes my friends,
People write many nasty experience they face in hospital or with doctors. Very few write their sweet experiences in hospital or with doctors.

So I thought to share my excellent sweet experience with a small, faraway hospital but with exceptional expertise in the field of knee replacement and other orthopedic and neurological complication.

My wife Operated for knee replacement on 15th...At 11 in the morning (to 2.30 pm) including recovery time inside operation theatre...

Then shifted to ICU.
Operation was good, my wife was in jolly mood and smiling while coming out from OT after the replacement ... But after 2 hrs of shifting to ICU, the real pain started... Wife was crying like mad for pain... But through medication by 8 pm it has started reducing... and she slept.
Nxt day, 16th, morning no pain...and shifted to pvt room cabin. I also staying in the same room with her. Excellent clean cosy room with all necessary requirements like AC, TV, eye catching view from 4th floor Window, attached very clean bath (no balcony), clean and daily fresh linen.

17th.. Sr Doctors and physiotherapist started her to walk and bent the new knee to 90°...

This was regular exercise, bending knee to 90° and walking in the corridor with the help of walker and physiotherapist till 19th...

And on 19th all bandage and all drain-pipes ( 3 in total... For Blood to drain our excess blood at operated knee, one for urine, one at spinal joint to push different medicine ) removed and....
discharged in the afternoon by doctor...
Same day, 19th, came to home by evening.

She is recovering nicely.... Walking inside the flat with the help of walker... pain she feel very very rarely.

After 9th day from operation, today (24th March) was the first check up...and it is absolutely OK.
Infact, my wife walk through out the day in hospital alone with the help of walker.
Today, she has been allowed by doctor to move and do morning/evening walk with walker and asked for further check up after 15 days.
No medicine given except multivitamin for further recovery as she has no pain.

We are very very happy for the excellent smooth operation, expertise of doctors, quick recovery process with effective treatment, support of Jr. Doctors, Physiotherapist, Metron, Sisters, Brothers, room boy and aayas for 24×7 and overall management of the hospital.

Well behaved people....
No extra billing...

We, and no one, before surgery, expected that after operation on 2nd day pain would vanish... she would walk and bend knee to 90°and get discharge on 4th day...!!!

All credit goes to Dr. Rahul Bade and his team including Anesthesists Dr. Ganesh Kolhe at Sparsh Multi-Speciality Hospital.

Thank you...well done, doctor !!!
🙏🙏🙏

Thanks to Lt. Col Dr Amogh Yadav from Mumbai and Dr. Rahul Mane for strongly recomanding us the hospital.

(Note : Treatment was going on at Sanchiti Hospital. But operated at Sparsh Multi Speciality Hospital)

featured_reviews.name: Sil Fun
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very important pro tip when ordering food from the canteen on the ground floor of this hospital:

If you have permission to eat on the upper floors where medical tests are conducted, because your family member cannot come down to the ground floor, do not tell any canteen staff that you are taking the food upstairs. Also, if you order a large amount of food, act as if your family member is sitting somewhere on the ground floor.

The reason is that the person who hands out food trays may refuse to give you a tray. In my experience, he created unnecessary problems for me.

After ordering more than ₹500 worth of food, he insisted that I eat the patties first and then the pizza and pasta later. I told him to give me everything at once. I also honestly informed him that my brother was upstairs as a patient undergoing tests and that we had permission to eat there.

I assumed he was trying to help, but after making me wait 20–30 minutes, when it was finally time to collect my order, he told me that trays were not allowed on the upper floors. He could have told me this before taking the order, but he didn't. It felt as though he waited until the food was ready because he thought I might cancel the order otherwise.

What's the point of allowing food to be taken upstairs if trays are not allowed? It seemed like an unnecessary rule that only created problems.

I eventually took the food upstairs without a tray. It was difficult because the plates were much smaller. My brother, who could barely walk properly, and I tried our best not to drop any food on the floor. However, crumbs from the patties and corn from the pizza still fell because the plates were too small for carrying so much food.

Hinduja Hospital, we visited your hospital for tests for my brother that cost around ₹10,000. Everyone on the upper floors—including the doctors, nurses, and reception staff—was professional, friendly, and helpful.

However, I am giving this review 1 star.

I am 29 years old, and this is the first time in my life that I have given anyone a 1-star review. Unfortunately, your canteen employee on the ground floor—the person handling payments, food distribution, and trays—left such a poor impression that it overshadowed an otherwise positive experience.

This incident happened in June 2025. I am writing this review a year later because I still remember how I was treated and how frustrating the experience was.

Dr. Vijay Bang meticulously performed a re-angiogram and utilized an FFR (Fractional Flow Reserve) test to assess the exact nature of the blockage. His precise diagnosis revealed that the blockage was only 30-40%, saving her from unnecessary invasive procedures.

​Later, when my mother had to be readmitted due to a critically high CRP (C-Reactive Protein) count, Dr. Bang immediately identified the issue, put her on the right medication, and successfully brought the levels down. Dr. Vijay Bang is not just an exceptionally skilled interventional cardiologist, but also a deeply compassionate professional. The world-class care at Lilavati Hospital, combined with his expertise, gave our family immense peace of mind. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.review_text:
We had purchased Midazolam Nasal Spray from General Medical(Colaba) on 31st Dec 2024 since my dad was getting epileptic seizures on stop on that day. Since we were in a hurry, we didn't wait for the bill which was our bad luck.  Unfortunately my dad passed on 08 Jan 2025. I went to General Medical last week to return the nasal spray which has not been opened only to be told that they won't accept the medicine since it was an open box. I was quite taken by surprise at their attitude. The medicine has their sticker with the price on it. This is the first time that I have been told that a medicine sold in a box can not be returned. A chemist called Mukesh told me outright that he wouldn't take it. An extremely rude man. I told him that I was returning it unopened since my father had passed. It didn't even remotely make a difference. Mukesh knew he was wrong and when I asked him his last name he didn't divulge the same. I went there around 4.30 pm and when I asked for the manager he lied and told me that he has gone for lunch. The strangest thing is that my late father was a regular over there and even that did not make any difference to that obnoxious man.

A STRONG MESSAGE TO GENERAL MEDICAL - YOUR PEOPLE NEED TO BE A BIT MORE SENSITIVE TO CUSTOMERS. IF A CUSTOMER HAS NOT UTILISED ANY MEDICINE AND WISHES TO RETURN IT EVEN WITHOUT A BILL, YOU NEED TO TAKE IT BACK ESPECIALLY IF YOUR COMPANY'S STICKER IS ON THE BOX.
